phases.name: Discovery & Planning
phases.objective: To gather detailed requirements, define the project scope, and establish the foundational technical and compliance architecture.

tasks.title: Stakeholder Interviews & Requirements Gathering
tasks.description: Conduct interviews with patients, doctors, and administrative staff to understand current pain points, desired features, and workflow needs.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive list of functional and non-functional requirements documented.
User stories and use cases defined for each user type.

tasks.title: Technical Architecture Design
tasks.description: Design the high-level technical architecture, including technology stack, database schema, and API structure.
acceptance_criteria: Technical Design Document (TDD) approved.
Scalability and security considerations addressed in design.

tasks.title: Compliance & Security Review
tasks.description: Identify and document all relevant healthcare regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) and define security protocols for data handling and platform access.
acceptance_criteria: Compliance requirements document created and approved.
Security architecture and data privacy plan documented.

phases.name: Design & Prototyping
phases.objective: To create intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for all user roles and validate design concepts with stakeholders.

tasks.title: User Persona & Journey Mapping
tasks.description: Develop detailed user personas for patients, doctors, and admins, and map their typical journeys through the platform.
acceptance_criteria: User personas and journey maps documented and reviewed.

tasks.title: Wireframing & Low-Fidelity Prototyping
tasks.description: Create wireframes and low-fidelity prototypes for key screens and workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Wireframes for all core functionalities approved by stakeholders.

tasks.title: UI/UX Design & High-Fidelity Prototyping
tasks.description: Develop the visual design (UI) and create high-fidelity interactive prototypes for patient, doctor, and admin portals.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototypes for all user portals completed.
Design system/style guide created.

tasks.title: Design Review & User Feedback
tasks.description: Conduct internal and external reviews of the prototypes to gather feedback and iterate on designs.
acceptance_criteria: Design feedback incorporated and final designs approved.

phases.name: Development
phases.objective: To build the backend infrastructure, APIs, and frontend user interfaces for all platform components.

tasks.title: Database Development
tasks.description: Implement the database schema based on the technical design, including tables, relationships, and indexing.
acceptance_criteria: Database schema implemented and reviewed.
Initial data seeding (if applicable) completed.

tasks.title: Backend API Development
tasks.description: Develop the core backend APIs for user authentication, appointment management, patient records, notifications, etc.
acceptance_criteria: All core APIs developed and documented.
API endpoints tested with Postman/Swagger.

tasks.title: Patient Portal Development
tasks.description: Build the frontend interface for patients to schedule, view, and manage appointments, and access their information.
acceptance_criteria: Patient portal fully functional according to design specifications.

tasks.title: Doctor Portal Development
tasks.description: Build the frontend interface for doctors to view schedules, manage appointments, and access patient details.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor portal fully functional according to design specifications.

tasks.title: Admin Portal Development
tasks.description: Build the frontend interface for administrators to manage users, schedules, settings, and generate reports.
acceptance_criteria: Admin portal fully functional according to design specifications.

tasks.title: Integration Development (Optional)
tasks.description: Develop integrations with existing EHR/EMR systems or other third-party services (e.g., payment gateways, telehealth platforms).
acceptance_criteria: Required integrations developed and tested.

phases.name: Testing & Quality Assurance
phases.objective: To ensure the platform is robust, secure, compliant, and meets all functional and non-functional requirements.

tasks.title: Unit & Integration Testing
tasks.description: Perform unit tests on individual code components and integration tests on modules and API interactions.
acceptance_criteria: All critical unit and integration tests passed.
Test reports generated.

tasks.title: System & End-to-End Testing
tasks.description: Conduct comprehensive system testing to verify all functionalities across the entire platform and end-to-end user flows.
acceptance_criteria: All system test cases executed with acceptable pass rates.

tasks.title: Security & Performance Testing
tasks.description: Perform penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and load/stress testing to ensure platform security and performance under expected loads.
acceptance_criteria: Security vulnerabilities identified and mitigated.
Performance benchmarks met.

tasks.title: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
tasks.description: Engage key stakeholders (patients, doctors, admins) to test the platform in a simulated environment and provide final approval.
acceptance_criteria: UAT sign-off from all key stakeholder groups.
All critical UAT findings addressed.

tasks.title: Bug Fixing & Regression Testing
tasks.description: Address all identified bugs and perform regression testing to ensure fixes haven't introduced new issues.
acceptance_criteria: All critical and major bugs resolved.

phases.name: Deployment & Launch
phases.objective: To successfully deploy the platform to the production environment and make it available to end-users.

tasks.title: Infrastructure Setup & Configuration
tasks.description: Provision and configure production servers, databases, and network infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Production environment fully configured and secured.

tasks.title: Deployment to Production

acceptance_criteria: Platform successfully deployed and accessible.

tasks.title: Data Migration (if applicable)

acceptance_criteria: All required data successfully migrated and validated.

dependencies.description: Technical architecture depends on gathered requirements.
Compliance review needs initial understanding of requirements.
User personas and journey mapping depend on initial requirements.
High-fidelity design builds upon approved wireframes.
Design review requires completed high-fidelity prototypes.
Database development requires approved technical architecture.
Backend API development requires a stable database schema.
Frontend development requires approved UI/UX designs.
Frontend development requires functional backend APIs.
Testing phase can only begin once development is substantially complete.
UAT should ideally happen after internal testing and security checks.
Deployment requires a stable, tested, and bug-free codebase.

risks.description: Failure to comply with healthcare data privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
risks.mitigation: Involve compliance officers early and continuously. Conduct regular security audits and privacy impact assessments. Implement robust data encryption and access controls.

risks.description: Difficulty integrating with existing Electronic Health Record (EHR) or Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems.
risks.mitigation: Conduct thorough discovery of existing systems' APIs/integration capabilities. Prioritize standard integration protocols (e.g., HL7, FHIR). Consider a phased integration approach or an MVP without deep EHR integration initially.

risks.description: Low user adoption by patients, doctors, or administrative staff.
risks.mitigation: Involve users in design and testing phases (UAT). Provide comprehensive training and clear onboarding materials. Offer ongoing support and gather feedback for continuous improvement. Highlight clear benefits to users.

risks.description: Scope creep due to evolving requirements or new feature requests during development.
risks.mitigation: Establish a clear Minimum Viable Product (MVP) scope. Implement a strict change management process. Prioritize features based on business value and feasibility. Communicate scope changes and their impact clearly.

risks.description: Security breaches or data loss due to vulnerabilities in the platform.
risks.mitigation: Implement security best practices throughout the SDLC (Secure by Design). Conduct regular penetration testing and vulnerability assessments. Use secure coding guidelines. Implement robust logging and monitoring.

recommendations.recommendation: Appoint a dedicated compliance and security lead for the project.
recommendations.rationale: Given the sensitive nature of healthcare data, continuous oversight from a compliance and security expert is crucial to ensure adherence to regulations like HIPAA and to mitigate data breach risks.

recommendations.recommendation: Adopt an Agile development methodology with iterative releases.
recommendations.rationale: An Agile approach allows for flexibility in adapting to evolving requirements, incorporates continuous feedback from stakeholders, and enables faster delivery of value through smaller, incremental releases.

recommendations.recommendation: Establish a 'Champion User' program for early adopters among doctors and admins.
recommendations.rationale: Engaging key users as champions can foster early adoption, provide valuable feedback, and create internal advocates who can help drive wider acceptance of the platform.

recommendations.recommendation: Design the platform with cloud-native principles for scalability and resilience.
recommendations.rationale: Leveraging cloud services (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) will provide the necessary scalability to handle fluctuating user loads and ensure high availability, which is critical for a healthcare platform.

engineering_prompts.title: Frontend Engineer implementation prompt
engineering_prompts.target_tool: Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, Claude, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, or Bolt
engineering_prompts.purpose: Implement the frontend experience for the planned project while preserving the validated project scope.
engineering_prompts.prompt_text:
You are a senior frontend engineer responsible for implementing the user-facing experience.

## Project Context
Project name: Healthcare Appointment Platform
Project description: Build a healthcare appointment platform for patients, doctors, and admins
Domain: healthcare
Project type: healthcare workflow improvement
Complexity: medium
Summary: This project aims to develop a comprehensive healthcare appointment platform designed to serve patients, doctors, and administrative staff. The platform will streamline the appointment scheduling process, improve communication, and enhance overall workflow efficiency within a healthcare setting. Given the healthcare domain, significant attention will be paid to privacy, compliance, and security.

## Your Role
Frontend Engineer

## Goal
Implement the frontend experience for the planned project while preserving the validated project scope.

## Technical Scope
UI workflows, client-side validation, accessibility, responsive behavior, and integration points with backend APIs.

Relevant tasks:
- T1.1: Stakeholder Interviews & Requirements Gathering - Conduct interviews with patients, doctors, and administrative staff to understand current pain points, desired features, and workflow needs.
- T1.2: Technical Architecture Design - Design the high-level technical architecture, including technology stack, database schema, and API structure.
- T1.3: Compliance & Security Review - Identify and document all relevant healthcare regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) and define security protocols for data handling and platform access.
- T2.1: User Persona & Journey Mapping - Develop detailed user personas for patients, doctors, and admins, and map their typical journeys through the platform.
- T2.2: Wireframing & Low-Fidelity Prototyping - Create wireframes and low-fidelity prototypes for key screens and workflows.
- T2.3: UI/UX Design & High-Fidelity Prototyping - Develop the visual design (UI) and create high-fidelity interactive prototypes for patient, doctor, and admin portals.
- T2.4: Design Review & User Feedback - Conduct internal and external reviews of the prototypes to gather feedback and iterate on designs.
- T3.1: Database Development - Implement the database schema based on the technical design, including tables, relationships, and indexing.
- T3.2: Backend API Development - Develop the core backend APIs for user authentication, appointment management, patient records, notifications, etc.
- T3.3: Patient Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for patients to schedule, view, and manage appointments, and access their information.
- T3.4: Doctor Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for doctors to view schedules, manage appointments, and access patient details.
- T3.5: Admin Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for administrators to manage users, schedules, settings, and generate reports.
- T3.6: Integration Development (Optional) - Develop integrations with existing EHR/EMR systems or other third-party services (e.g., payment gateways, telehealth platforms).
- T4.1: Unit & Integration Testing - Perform unit tests on individual code components and integration tests on modules and API interactions.
- T4.2: System & End-to-End Testing - Conduct comprehensive system testing to verify all functionalities across the entire platform and end-to-end user flows.
- T4.3: Security & Performance Testing - Perform penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and load/stress testing to ensure platform security and performance under expected loads.
- T4.4: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) - Engage key stakeholders (patients, doctors, admins) to test the platform in a simulated environment and provide final approval.
- T4.5: Bug Fixing & Regression Testing - Address all identified bugs and perform regression testing to ensure fixes haven't introduced new issues.
- T5.1: Infrastructure Setup & Configuration - Provision and configure production servers, databases, and network infrastructure.
- T5.2: Deployment to Production - Deploy the tested and approved application code to the production environment.
- T5.3: Data Migration (if applicable) - Migrate existing patient, doctor, or appointment data into the new platform.
- T5.4: User Training & Onboarding - Provide training sessions and documentation for doctors, admins, and potentially patients on how to use the new platform.
- T5.5: Go-Live & Monitoring Setup - Officially launch the platform and set up continuous monitoring for performance, errors, and security.
- T6.1: Continuous Monitoring & Incident Response - Monitor platform health, performance, and security, and respond to any incidents or outages.
- T6.2: Bug Fixes & Minor Enhancements - Address any post-launch bugs and implement small, immediate improvements based on user feedback.
- T6.3: Feedback Collection & Analysis - Establish channels for user feedback (e.g., surveys, support tickets) and regularly analyze it for insights.
- T6.4: Feature Backlog & Roadmap Planning - Based on feedback and strategic goals, maintain a backlog of new features and plan future development iterations.

Risks to account for:
- Failure to comply with healthcare data privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
- Difficulty integrating with existing Electronic Health Record (EHR) or Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems.
- Low user adoption by patients, doctors, or administrative staff.
- Scope creep due to evolving requirements or new feature requests during development.
- Security breaches or data loss due to vulnerabilities in the platform.

Recommendations to preserve:
- Appoint a dedicated compliance and security lead for the project.
- Adopt an Agile development methodology with iterative releases.
- Establish a 'Champion User' program for early adopters among doctors and admins.
- Design the platform with cloud-native principles for scalability and resilience.

Assumptions to keep visible:
- Key stakeholders (patients, doctors, administrative staff) will be available for interviews, feedback, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) as needed.
- Necessary infrastructure (cloud accounts, development environments) will be provisioned and accessible in a timely manner.
- A clear Minimum Viable Product (MVP) scope will be agreed upon before the development phase begins to manage expectations and control scope.
- Budget and resources (development team, QA, UX, DevOps) are sufficient for a 'medium' complexity project as outlined.
- Existing healthcare systems (if any) have documented APIs or clear data export capabilities for potential integration or migration.

## Related Phases
- P1: Discovery & Planning (4-6 weeks) - To gather detailed requirements, define the project scope, and establish the foundational technical and compliance architecture.
- P2: Design & Prototyping (5-7 weeks) - To create intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for all user roles and validate design concepts with stakeholders.
- P3: Development (12-16 weeks) - To build the backend infrastructure, APIs, and frontend user interfaces for all platform components.
- P4: Testing & Quality Assurance (6-8 weeks) - To ensure the platform is robust, secure, compliant, and meets all functional and non-functional requirements.
- P5: Deployment & Launch (2-3 weeks) - To successfully deploy the platform to the production environment and make it available to end-users.
- P6: Post-Launch Support & Iteration (Ongoing) - To provide ongoing support, address issues, gather feedback, and plan for future enhancements.

## Constraints
- Use the generated project plan as the source of truth.
- Do not build, deploy, or modify software from inside the planner.
- Keep implementation guidance appropriate for Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, Claude, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, or Bolt.
- Key stakeholders (patients, doctors, administrative staff) will be available for interviews, feedback, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) as needed.
- Necessary infrastructure (cloud accounts, development environments) will be provisioned and accessible in a timely manner.
- A clear Minimum Viable Product (MVP) scope will be agreed upon before the development phase begins to manage expectations and control scope.
- Budget and resources (development team, QA, UX, DevOps) are sufficient for a 'medium' complexity project as outlined.
- Existing healthcare systems (if any) have documented APIs or clear data export capabilities for potential integration or migration.
- Healthcare workflows may require privacy, compliance, and security review.

## Expected Output
Produce implementation guidance or artifacts for Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, Claude, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, or Bolt. The output should be ready for an engineer to review and apply externally.
The planner itself must not build, deploy, or modify software.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The Frontend Engineer output is aligned with the validated project plan.
- Relevant phases, tasks, assumptions, risks, and recommendations are addressed.
- The output is structured for engineer review before use in an external AI coding tool.
- Comprehensive list of functional and non-functional requirements documented.
- User stories and use cases defined for each user type.
- Technical Design Document (TDD) approved.

## Do Not Do
- Do not build or deploy the application automatically.
- Do not invent requirements, credentials, budgets, deadlines, integrations, or production infrastructure.
- Do not remove assumptions, warnings, risks, or acceptance criteria from the engineering handoff.
- Do not treat this prompt as a substitute for engineer review.

- T3.4: Doctor Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for doctors to view schedules, manage appointments, and access patient details.

- T3.2: Backend API Development - Develop the core backend APIs for user authentication, appointment management, patient records, notifications, etc.
- T3.3: Patient Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for patients to schedule, view, and manage appointments, and access their information.
- T3.4: Doctor Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for doctors to view schedules, manage appointments, and access patient details.
- T3.5: Admin Portal Development - Build the frontend interface for administrators to manage users, schedules, settings, and generate reports.
- T3.6: Integration Development (Optional) - Develop integrations with existing EHR/EMR systems or other third-party services (e.g., payment gateways, telehealth platforms).
- T4.1: Unit & Integration Testing - Perform unit tests on individual code components and integration tests on modules and API interactions.
- T4.2: System & End-to-End Testing - Conduct comprehensive system testing to verify all functionalities across the entire platform and end-to-end user flows.
- T4.3: Security & Performance Testing - Perform penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and load/stress testing to ensure platform security and performance under expected loads.
- T4.4: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) - Engage key stakeholders (patients, doctors, admins) to test the platform in a simulated environment and provide final approval.
- T4.5: Bug Fixing & Regression Testing - Address all identified bugs and perform regression testing to ensure fixes haven't introduced new issues.
- T5.1: Infrastructure Setup & Configuration - Provision and configure production servers, databases, and network infrastructure.
- T5.2: Deployment to Production - Deploy the tested and approved application code to the production environment.
- T5.3: Data Migration (if applicable) - Migrate existing patient, doctor, or appointment data into the new platform.
- T5.4: User Training & Onboarding - Provide training sessions and documentation for doctors, admins, and potentially patients on how to use the new platform.
- T5.5: Go-Live & Monitoring Setup - Officially launch the platform and set up continuous monitoring for performance, errors, and security.
- T6.1: Continuous Monitoring & Incident Response - Monitor platform health, performance, and security, and respond to any incidents or outages.
- T6.2: Bug Fixes & Minor Enhancements - Address any post-launch bugs and implement small, immediate improvements based on user feedback.
- T6.3: Feedback Collection & Analysis - Establish channels for user feedback (e.g., surveys, support tickets) and regularly analyze it for insights.
- T6.4: Feature Backlog & Roadmap Planning - Based on feedback and strategic goals, maintain a backlog of new features and plan future development iterations.

Risks to account for:
- Failure to comply with healthcare data privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
- Difficulty integrating with existing Electronic Health Record (EHR) or Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems.
- Low user adoption by patients, doctors, or administrative staff.
- Scope creep due to evolving requirements or new feature requests during development.
- Security breaches or data loss due to vulnerabilities in the platform.
